queries.diagnose: The untrained mind runs like the wind, replaying and imagining; left to itself it becomes its own enemy.
queries.steady: Praise and blame, success and failure, come and go like the wind; the self that is steady remains when the mind is stormy.

verse.speaker: Arjuna
verse.setting: Arjuna confesses the mind is as hard to hold as the wind; Krishna answers.
verse.sanskrit: चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम् । तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम् ॥
verse.line: The mind is restless, stormy, stubborn and strong. Holding it feels like holding the wind.
verse.translation: For the mind is restless, Krishna, turbulent, powerful and stubborn. I think it is as hard to hold as the wind.
verse.why: The mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go train it.

prasang.title: Mastering the mind
prasang.summary: Arjuna says the mind is restless, stormy and stubborn. Krishna agrees, and says practice and letting go can train it.
prasang.lesson: The mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go train it.

verse.meaning: Arjuna tells Krishna that his mind is like the wind. It is restless, stormy and stubborn. He says holding it feels impossible. Krishna agrees. He says the mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go can train it. The truth is that the mind wants to run. Yet it can be steadied not by force, but by the quiet habit of returning to it, again and again.
verse.for_you: You sit with the phone and the mind spins. You do not need to win a battle with it today. Just notice that the mind is stormy. That is what it does. Your job is not to force it still.

verse.speaker: Rama
verse.setting: Rama describes his restless mind to the sages.
verse.sanskrit: चेतः पतति कार्येषु विहगः स्वामिषेष्विव । क्षणेन विरतिं याति बालः क्रीडनकादिव ॥
verse.line: The mind pounces on a task like a bird on food, then drops it like a bored child's toy.
verse.translation: The mind swoops onto tasks like a bird onto meat, and a moment later loses interest, like a child with a toy.
verse.why: Naming honestly what feels empty is the first step; Rama's lament is a question, not the answer.

prasang.title: Rama's lament: what is the point of all this?
prasang.summary: Asked to speak, Rama pours out what he has seen: wealth hardens people, life drips away like water off a leaf, ego and craving run us, the mind never fills, childhood, youth and old age each bring their own suffering, and time eats everything. He ends by saying only the company of good people gives him hope.
prasang.story_hook: In front of the whole court, the young prince stood up and said what everyone feels and nobody says.
prasang.lesson: Naming honestly what feels empty is the first step; Rama's lament is a question, not the answer.

verse.meaning: Rama tells the sages that his mind is like a bird. It swoops onto a task, then drops it. It is like a child with a toy. He sees that nothing fills the mind. He names what feels empty. He does not yet know the way out. He only knows that the mind is hungry and restless.
verse.for_you: You move from one app to the next. The mind is hungry and nothing satisfies it. You do not need to fix this hunger today. Just name it. See that the mind is restless because it has no quiet place to rest.

verse.speaker: Yama
verse.sanskrit: यस्त्वविज्ञानवान्भवत्ययुक्तेन मनसा सदा । तस्येन्द्रियाण्यवश्यानि दुष्टाश्वा इव सारथेः ॥ यस्तु विज्ञानवान्भवति युक्तेन मनसा सदा । तस्येन्द्रियाणि वश्यानि सदश्वा इव सारथेः ॥
verse.line: Without understanding, the senses bolt like wild horses; with a steady mind, they run like trained ones.
verse.translation: For one who lacks understanding, whose mind is never held steady, the senses run out of control like a driver's wild horses. For one who has understanding, whose mind is always steady, the senses obey like good horses.
verse.why: Hold the reins of your mind, or your senses will drive for you.

prasang.title: The chariot of the self
prasang.summary: Yama pictures a person as a chariot: the self is the rider, the body the chariot, the intellect the driver, the mind the reins and the senses the horses. With a steady mind the horses obey; without it they bolt. He ends with the call to arise and wake.
prasang.lesson: Hold the reins of your mind, or your senses will drive for you.

verse.meaning: Yama tells Nachiketa about the chariot of the self. The senses are the horses. The mind is the reins. Without a steady mind, the horses run wild. With a steady mind, they run as they should. The self is the rider. The body is the chariot. The mind holds the reins. If the mind is not steady, the senses drive the person. The person must hold the reins of the mind.
verse.for_you: Your eyes move across the screen because your mind is not steady. You do not need to pull back the horses today. You only need to notice the reins. Feel the phone in your hand. Feel the breath. That is the reins. Hold them for a moment.

verse.speaker: Ribhu
verse.sanskrit: यानि दुःखानि या तृष्णा दुःसहा ये दुराधयः । शान्तचेतःसु तत्सर्वं तमोऽर्केष्विव नश्यति ॥
verse.line: Sorrow, craving and unbearable anxiety all vanish in a calm mind, like darkness before the sun.
verse.translation: Whatever sorrows, whatever craving, whatever unbearable anxieties there are, all of them vanish in calm minds, as darkness vanishes before the sun.
verse.why: Start with calm or contentment, and the rest follows.

prasang.title: Ribhu on calm and contentment
prasang.summary: Ribhu answers Nidagha: freedom has four gatekeepers (calm, inquiry, contentment and good company), and winning one brings the rest. In a calm mind sorrow and anxiety vanish; restlessness is simply the mind's nature, and only your own mind can lift you out.
prasang.lesson: Start with calm or contentment, and the rest follows.

verse.meaning: Ribhu tells Nidagha that sorrow, craving and unbearable anxiety all vanish in a calm mind, as darkness vanishes before the sun. Ribhu teaches that freedom has four gatekeepers: calm, inquiry, contentment and good company. Winning one brings the rest. Restlessness is simply the mind's nature, and only your own mind can lift you out of it.
verse.for_you: After a long day of screens, sit with the phone away and let the room be quiet. Let the mind rest in that silence. This is your first step toward calm, and calm is what dissolves the stress you feel.

verse.setting: Krishna teaches Arjuna how to meditate and what a settled mind is like.
verse.sanskrit: यतो यतो निश्चरति मनश्चञ्चलमस्थिरम् । ततस्ततो नियम्यैतदात्मन्येव वशं नयेत् ॥
verse.line: Wherever the restless mind wanders, gently bring it back. Again and again.
verse.translation: Wherever the restless, unsteady mind wanders, from there one should draw it back and bring it under the control of the self.
verse.why: Moderation and gentle return, again and again, settle the mind.

prasang.title: Meditation in detail
prasang.summary: Krishna describes meditation: moderation in food and sleep, the mind like a lamp in a windless place, bringing the wandering mind back, and feeling others' joy and pain as one's own.
prasang.lesson: Moderation and gentle return, again and again, settle the mind.

verse.meaning: Krishna teaches Arjuna that wherever the restless, unsteady mind wanders, from there one should draw it back and bring it under the control of the self. Krishna describes a settled mind as a lamp in a windless place, and teaches that moderation in food and sleep helps the mind settle.
verse.for_you: When your mind wanders to the next notification, gently bring it back to the book in front of you. Do this again and again. This gentle return is how the mind finds its footing.

verse.sanskrit: नित्याभ्यासविवेकाभ्यां चित्तमाशु प्रसीदति । आम्र एव दशामेति साहकारीं शनैः शनैः ॥

verse.translation: Through daily practice and discernment the mind soon becomes clear, just as a mango slowly ripens into its sweetness.
verse.why: Grace and effort work together; keep practising daily, and let the mind ripen slowly.

prasang.title: Prahlada: effort and grace are not rivals
prasang.summary: After telling how Prahlada awakened, Vasishtha faces Rama's challenge: if everything comes by effort, wasn't Prahlada saved by Vishnu's grace? Vasishtha answers that Prahlada earned it himself, that the Self and Vishnu are not two, and that sometimes we wake by our own effort and sometimes by grace reached through devotion. Steady daily practice ripens the mind like a mango.
prasang.lesson: Grace and effort work together; keep practising daily, and let the mind ripen slowly.

verse.meaning: Vasishtha tells Rama that through daily practice and discernment the mind soon becomes clear, just as a mango slowly ripens into its sweetness. Vasishtha explains that effort and grace work together, and that steady daily practice ripens the mind like a mango.
verse.for_you: Do not expect a sudden change. Let the mind ripen slowly, like a mango. Show up for your studies each day, and let the clarity come in its own time.

story.title: King Janaka overhears the sages and keeps ruling, with a free mind
story.story_hook: One spring morning, a king out for a walk overheard a song that he could not stop thinking about.
story.summary: Walking in his spring garden, King Janaka overhears hidden sages singing about the self. Shaken, he climbs to his palace roof and questions everything he has lived for. When his doorkeeper calls him to the day's work, he decides not to run away: he gets up and does his duties, but with a mind that no longer clutches.
story.lesson: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.

anchor.speaker: Janaka
anchor.setting: King Janaka, alone on his palace roof after overhearing wandering sages, rethinks his life.
anchor.sanskrit: संपदश्च विचित्रा यास्ताश्चेच्चित्तेन संमताः । तत्ता अपि महारम्भा हन्त मन्ये महापदः ॥ आपदोऽपि विचित्रा यास्ताश्चेन्मनसि संमताः । तत्ता अपि महारम्भा मन्ये मनसि संपदः ॥
anchor.line: Good fortune the mind clutches becomes trouble. Trouble the mind accepts becomes a kind of fortune.
anchor.translation: All those dazzling fortunes, if the mind clings to them, are really great calamities in grand disguise. And all those varied misfortunes, if the mind accepts them, are really fortunes.
anchor.why: You don't have to leave your life to change it. Do the day's work with a mind that doesn't clutch.
anchor.misuse: Accepting a hardship doesn't mean not fixing what can be fixed.

script: You are sitting there and the mind will not stop. It jumps from one thing to the next and you feel it in your chest. You sit with the phone and the mind spins. You do not need to win a battle with it today.

Arjuna has laid down his bow. He is looking at Krishna and he is honest about what is happening inside him. He says his mind is like the wind. It is restless and stormy and he cannot hold it still. Arjuna said:
चञ्चलं हि मनः कृष्ण प्रमाथि बलवद्दृढम्, तस्याहं निग्रहं मन्ये वायोरिव सुदुष्करम्.
In plain words: The mind is restless, stormy, stubborn and strong. Holding it feels like holding the wind.

Krishna does not argue with him. He agrees that the mind is powerful and stubborn. It wants to run. But he says it can be steadied. Not by force. By practice and letting go. This is easier said than done, because the mind will always want to chase the next thing.

When the phone is in your hand and the thoughts are racing, do not try to force them away. Just notice that the mind is stormy. That is what it does. Your part is to return to it, again and again, with quiet practice.
Can you let the wind blow for a moment?

depth.life: You pick up the phone and the mind keeps spinning. The hours pass and the stress sits in your chest. You are studying, but the screen is just a place for the mind to run. It feels like you are always behind, even when you are doing nothing.
depth.points: Arjuna tells Krishna that the mind is stormy, stubborn and strong. He does not say it is weak. He says it is as hard to hold as the wind. The mind is not your enemy. It is a force that needs to be understood, not conquered.
depth.practice: Set a timer for ten minutes. Put the phone down and let your eyes rest on one thing. Do not try to change your thoughts. Just let them be.
depth.question: What would it feel like to let the mind run for ten minutes without trying to hold it?
